evidence.claim: Biden and Kishida announced removal of HEU from three Japanese sites, reducing weapons-usable material.
evidence.title: U.S. removes over 30 kilograms of highly enriched uranium from Japan
evidence.publisher: Department of Energy, National Nuclear Security Administration
evidence.excerpt: Biden and Kishida announced removal of HEU from three Japanese sites, reducing weapons-usable material.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official nonproliferation action with direct presidential attribution.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Biden's nonproliferation diplomacy with Japan.
contrary_evidence: This is a discrete risk-reduction success, not a broad disarmament settlement.

evidence.claim: The P5 statement affirmed that nuclear war cannot be won, called nuclear weapons defensive, and committed to strengthen measures against unauthorized or unintended use.
evidence.title: Joint Statement by the United Nations Security Council Permanent Members on Preventing Nuclear War and Avoiding Arms Races
evidence.excerpt: The P5 statement affirmed that nuclear war cannot be won, called nuclear weapons defensive, and committed to strengthen measures against unauthorized or unintended use.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential archive of a joint nuclear-risk statement involving the United States.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable as part of Biden's joined P5 nuclear stance.
contrary_evidence: It is a joint statement, so attribution is shared with other nuclear powers.

evidence.claim: Biden reaffirmed the U.S. commitment to Article 5 and NATO ally security while discussing support for Ukraine and reduced dependence on Russian energy.
evidence.title: Readout of President Biden's Meeting with President Andrzej Duda of Poland
evidence.excerpt: Biden reaffirmed the U.S. commitment to Article 5 and NATO ally security while discussing support for Ukraine and reduced dependence on Russian energy.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official presidential readout reproduced in the archive.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the Ukraine crisis in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Biden's alliance signaling and crisis management.
contrary_evidence: Alliance reassurance is indirect evidence for nuclear responsibility rather than a direct command-and-control act.

evidence.claim: The U.S. said it would work with the IAEA on AUKUS safeguards and maintain open and transparent engagement on nonproliferation standards.
evidence.title: Under Secretary Jenkins' Remarks at the U.S. Press Conference on U.S. Goals and Priorities for the IAEA General Conference
evidence.excerpt: The U.S. said it would work with the IAEA on AUKUS safeguards and maintain open and transparent engagement on nonproliferation standards.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official administration remarks, but the page was inaccessible directly and only the search snippet was available here.
evidence.period_fit: Late 2022 context for dual-use and safeguards policy.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Administration-level policy under Biden, though not a direct Biden speech.
contrary_evidence: AUKUS also raised proliferation concerns among critics.

evidence.claim: The CTBT bans nuclear weapon test explosions everywhere and is a core part of the nuclear arms control and disarmament framework.
evidence.title: Ending Nuclear Test Explosions
evidence.excerpt: The CTBT bans nuclear weapon test explosions everywhere and is a core part of the nuclear arms control and disarmament framework.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Authoritative treaty-body explanation of the treaty's purpose and verification logic.
evidence.period_fit: General treaty context relevant to Biden's 2022 nonproliferation posture.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Context only, not a direct Biden act.
contrary_evidence: This source explains treaty context and does not attribute a specific Biden decision.

evidence.claim: SIPRI reported that the United States and Russia continued modernizing their nuclear arsenals and that global reductions of operational warheads had stalled.
evidence.title: 10. World nuclear forces
evidence.excerpt: SIPRI reported that the United States and Russia continued modernizing their nuclear arsenals and that global reductions of operational warheads had stalled.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent technical assessment by a leading research institute using open-source estimates.
evidence.period_fit: Directly relevant to the 2022 inherited baseline.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Inherited strategic baseline and comparison context for Biden.
contrary_evidence: This is country-level baseline data, not a direct judgment on Biden's own decisions.

evidence.claim: SIPRI estimated that nearly 2000 warheads were kept in high operational alert, nearly all belonging to Russia or the USA, and said modernization would likely increase arsenals over the next decade.
evidence.title: Global nuclear arsenals are expected to grow as states continue to modernize - New SIPRI Yearbook out now
evidence.excerpt: SIPRI estimated that nearly 2000 warheads were kept in high operational alert, nearly all belonging to Russia or the USA, and said modernization would likely increase arsenals over the next decade.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent press release summarizing the institute's annual nuclear-forces assessment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Context only, not direct Biden conduct.
contrary_evidence: Modernization baseline does not itself prove deterioration or improvement under Biden.

evidence.claim: ACA argued the 2022 NPR preserved a dangerous reliance on the threat of nuclear use and missed opportunities to reduce nuclear risk.
evidence.title: Biden's Disappointing Nuclear Posture Review
evidence.excerpt: ACA argued the 2022 NPR preserved a dangerous reliance on the threat of nuclear use and missed opportunities to reduce nuclear risk.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent expert critique written after the NPR release and directly focused on the policy text.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly about Biden's final 2022 posture text.
contrary_evidence: The critique also acknowledges some movement toward arms control and risk reduction.

evidence.claim: ACA said Biden entered office intending to narrow the nuclear role, but institutional resistance made that goal difficult to realize cleanly.
evidence.title: The Biden Nuclear Posture Review: Obstacles to Reducing Reliance on Nuclear Weapons
evidence.excerpt: ACA said Biden entered office intending to narrow the nuclear role, but institutional resistance made that goal difficult to realize cleanly.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent analysis of the policy process and its constraints, but pre-finalization.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly about Biden's intended policy and the constraints around it.
contrary_evidence: This is a forecast and process analysis, not an outcome audit.

evidence.claim: FAS said the 2022 NPR resisted pressure to add new nuclear weapons and instead adjusted the existing force posture while integrating conventional and nuclear planning.
evidence.title: The 2022 Nuclear Posture Review: Arms Control Subdued By Military Rivalry
evidence.excerpt: FAS said the 2022 NPR resisted pressure to add new nuclear weapons and instead adjusted the existing force posture while integrating conventional and nuclear planning.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent nuclear-policy analysis by a leading technical source.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly about Biden's administration and the NPR it released.
contrary_evidence: The same analysis notes continuing military rivalry and not a decisive break from deterrence-heavy policy.

evidence.claim: Brookings said Biden had been comparatively cautious on nuclear policy, prioritized stability with other nuclear powers, and strengthened assurances to allies.
evidence.title: How would Trump and Biden handle US nuclear policy upon reelection?
evidence.excerpt: Brookings said Biden had been comparatively cautious on nuclear policy, prioritized stability with other nuclear powers, and strengthened assurances to allies.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent analytical assessment, but written retrospectively in 2024.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective over the Biden period, useful for synthesis but not primary evidence.
contrary_evidence: The same analysis says he maintained a robust deterrent rather than a purely arms-control posture.

evidence.claim: The Biden administration had been sending private warnings to Moscow for months about grave consequences if Russia used a nuclear weapon in Ukraine, while keeping the response deliberately vague.
evidence.title: U.S. has sent private warnings to Russia against using a nuclear weapon
evidence.excerpt: The Biden administration had been sending private warnings to Moscow for months about grave consequences if Russia used a nuclear weapon in Ukraine, while keeping the response deliberately vague.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous reporting based on U.S. officials on a live crisis issue.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Biden's crisis-management approach through administration channels.
contrary_evidence: The source relies on unnamed officials and does not disclose the private message content.

evidence.claim: The White House said Biden's Armageddon warning was not based on new intelligence and did not require a change in U.S. nuclear posture.
evidence.title: Biden's 'Armageddon' warning wasn't based on new intelligence, US says
evidence.excerpt: The White House said Biden's Armageddon warning was not based on new intelligence and did not require a change in U.S. nuclear posture.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous reporting that directly quotes the White House response to Biden's remarks.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Biden's rhetoric and the administration's response.
contrary_evidence: The remark was unusually stark and drew allied caution.

evidence.claim: CSIS argued the Biden administration would need integrated deterrence and integrated arms control to reduce nuclear risk effectively.
evidence.title: Reading the Nuclear Tea Leaves: Policy and Posture in the Biden Administration
evidence.excerpt: CSIS argued the Biden administration would need integrated deterrence and integrated arms control to reduce nuclear risk effectively.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specialized independent analysis of the Biden nuclear-policy process, though partly prospective.
evidence.period_fit: Early Biden context and process framing.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly about Biden's nuclear-policy approach and constraints.
contrary_evidence: This is analytic projection rather than a 2022 outcome audit.

evidence.claim: CSIS said the 2022 NPR did not adopt sole purpose but did retire some capabilities and emphasized that deterrence and risk reduction must coexist.
evidence.title: A New Nuclear Age?
evidence.excerpt: CSIS said the 2022 NPR did not adopt sole purpose but did retire some capabilities and emphasized that deterrence and risk reduction must coexist.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent synthesis that is later and broader than 2022, but still useful for retrospective calibration.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly about Biden-era policy in hindsight.
contrary_evidence: Retrospective synthesis is less direct than contemporaneous 2022 evidence.

unresolved_gaps: Direct 2022 command-and-control and safeguards evidence is thinner than the public nuclear rhetoric and treaty-posture record.
The strongest crisis evidence is mostly speeches and reported private warnings rather than a declassified operational de-escalation record.
Direct 2022 documentary evidence on private diplomacy, ceasefire channels, and partner-use limits remains thinner than the public sanctions and aid record.
National-level evidence on protest policing, retaliation for dissent, and the federal government's leverage over local police remains thinner than the anti-hate and gun-safety record.
Border-enforcement attribution is still mixed because a large share of the harmful conduct sits in inherited systems and sub-agency action.
Direct evidence on state-level election administration, intimidation, and coercive presidential leverage against opponents is still limited.
Household distribution by race, region, and income tier is thinner than the macro and legislative record.
The causal split between Biden-era policy, global shocks, and Federal Reserve tightening remains mixed.
Child care, disability services, and elder-care evidence is still thin compared with health, housing, food, and crisis-response coverage.
The housing record is strong on funding and program design but weaker on realized rent-burden and eviction-prevention outcomes in 2022.
Direct personal-nexus evidence on recusal, ethics waivers, family-business benefit, or obstruction of scrutiny remains thin.
The clearest negative pattern is repeated factual exaggeration in speeches, but the record lacks equally direct correction or retraction evidence.
Independent project-level verification of 2022 execution for CHIPS, IRA, and infrastructure remains thinner than the policy-architecture record.
Community-level outcomes for specific groups and regions are still not well verified in the package.
